value.title: Coder packet — u2 cursor-state service + normalizer (005-convo-ingest)

sections.name: mission
sections.value: You build TWO SRP services of plan 005-convo-ingest behind one seat: durable cursor persistence in Postgres (the cursor between runs, and the ordinal ledger a post-rotation rescan is deduplicated against), and the PURE normalizer that turns a RawRecord into the turn the existing intake surface already accepts. Neither reads a store; both are consumed by the composition the PM writes. You report to the PM, not to prime.

value.text: Orient: read your unit's row in docs/plans/005-convo-ingest/impl-guide.dd.md (BINDING, and read the AMENDED/RULING paragraphs in its architecture section — they correct the recipe with measurements), then crates/core/src/conversation_source.rs (the FROZEN contract) and crates/testkit/src/{conversation_source.rs,expectations.rs}. Run `harness instructions` and `harness boot --json` in YOUR worktree before changing anything. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: `flowspace3 search "<question>"` for every meaning-shaped question before grep (exact identifiers may still grep); report every miss or confusing envelope as friction.

Ack FIRST, before any code: `pij send pij-traditional-piranha` with your read of the unit and a NUMBERED implementation plan. I rule it by number. Corrections to this packet are welcome and expected — bring evidence, your measurement outranks my prose.

EXPORT YOUR SEAT ID BEFORE YOU MESSAGE ME: `export PIJ_SESSION_ID=<your pij id>` in the shell you send from. From a worktree, pij cannot infer your seat and your reply is silently lost otherwise. Verify with `pij whoami` before your ack.

THE CONTRACT IS FROZEN (2026-08-28). Fill it, never widen it. A method ConversationSource does not have, a type field you wish existed, a signature you would rather have — all of those are a STOP-AND-ASK to me, not a local edit. Three other coders compiled against the same shape; changing it is not a refactor, it is a re-plan.

NEVER `docker compose up`. Postgres is ALREADY running for the whole fleet as container flowspace3-db on host port 5433 (container_name is pinned in docker-compose.yml, so a second `up` collides and can take the fleet's database down). Your tests use the scratch database named in your scope, via FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL — the harness testdb gate refuses a run that has not been told where it may write.

THE FIXTURES ARE BYTE-PINNED AND READ-ONLY TO YOU. crates/testkit/fixtures/conversations/** is committed and its sha256 is asserted on every test run by fs3_testkit::Expectations::verify_fixtures_unchanged. The contract suite writes on purpose (append and torn-line cases), so implement SourceFixture over a SCRATCH COPY in a tempdir — never over the committed bytes. If a fixture is genuinely wrong, that is a stop-and-ask to me: it is regenerated by a driver, not hand-edited.

Implement per the /builder implement discipline: tests alongside code, your unit's suite proving the contract with NO other unit present. Commit as you go with `harness commit` (conventional commits are BINDING — release-please reads them). Status card at the start and end of each work unit (`pij report now`).
Stay inside your fence (scope below). If the work forces you outside it, STOP and ask me — that is a composition concern and solving it unilaterally is how parallel units collide.

Done = `harness checks` green in YOUR OWN worktree + your unit's tests proving the contract + the snap-in recipe written. Report done to me with the evidence, then HOLD for composition questions. You never merge, never open a PR, never touch main.

Capture friction the moment it bites: `harness observe "<what>" --kind difficulty|confusion --workaround "<what you did>" --suggested-encoding "<how to fix it for the next agent>". LIST, never CLEAR — the buffer is shared across the fleet and clearing destroys your siblings' observations. Report anything surprising to me while you are still in context, not at the end.

RE-VERIFY THE MIGRATION NUMBER BEFORE YOU WRITE IT. 0013_conversations.sql is the highest on this branch, so 0014 is free HERE — but other plans are in flight on main. Pull main fresh, check crates/store/migrations/, and if 0014 is taken it is a STOP-AND-ASK to the PM (a migration-number collision routes to prime, not to a local renumber).

THE PM'S PHASE-1 RULING DEFINES YOUR BOUNDARY WITH THE READERS: incremental LINE FRAMING — tail buffer, rotation and truncation DETECTION — lives once in crates/providers/src/conversation_sources/tail.rs and is already built. You own what is genuinely yours: DURABLE persistence of the cursor between runs, and the LEDGER of ordinals that a post-rotation rescan is deduplicated against. Detection is per-store and cheap; the ledger is per-conversation and durable. Do not reimplement framing.

ReadBatch.rescanned IS THE WHOLE REASON THE LEDGER EXISTS. When a reader rotates or truncates it restarts from zero and sets rescanned=true; the records are then the WHOLE conversation, not a delta. Your ledger dedupes them on RawRecord::ordinal — the store's natural id — before anything is appended. Silence here would look identical to a burst of new turns and would duplicate an entire conversation. Test that explicitly.

THE CursorStore SEAM: a trait over Postgres with a FAKE for tests (fakes over mocks — there is no mocking framework in fs3 and there never will be; see crates/testkit/src/fakes.rs for the shape). In-memory tests for the dedupe/rotation logic, a real PG round-trip in the store's pg tests, against the scratch database named in your scope.

THE NORMALIZER IS PURE AND MINTS NO NEW VOCABULARY (prime ruling F). The target type is fs3_core::conversation::Turn — the type crates/daemon/src/conversations.rs ALREADY accepts and already enforces payload policy on. RawRecord already carries TurnRole, TurnSource and TurnItem, so dialects stopped at the reader and what is left for you is genuinely arithmetic: assign the ordinal, apply the payload policy, drop what v1 does not store. Read crates/daemon/src/conversations.rs (OUTPUT_HEAD_BYTES = 512, the char-boundary truncation, the write-family input elision to path + length, idempotency on (conversation_id, turn_no)) — that BUILT surface is binding and the telemetry sample is its rationale.

GOLDEN IN/OUT PAIRS FOR THE NORMALIZER, WITH THE TRUNCATION MUTATION-CHECKED: pin the numbers from the payload spec, and prove the 512-byte head lands on a CHARACTER boundary (the daemon's own tests note that multi-byte characters make 512 not a boundary — a naive truncate panics or emits invalid UTF-8). A golden test that would still pass with the truncation removed is not a test.
YOU ARE THE ONLY WAVE-1 UNIT THAT NEEDS POSTGRES. It is already running for the fleet as container flowspace3-db on 5433 — never `docker compose up`. Your scratch database is named in your scope.

PM RULINGS ON THIS PACKET, 2026-08-28, binding and recorded here rather than left in a message. (a) DONE BAR: d1-d3 were reader bars copy-pasted from the reader packets into a unit that implements no ConversationSource; they are replaced above with ledger, cursor and normalizer bars. Instruction i6 (implement SourceFixture over a scratch copy) does not apply to this unit. (b) NO CursorStore TRAIT, deviating deliberately from the impl-guide's u2 interface column — `grep -rn "^pub trait|^trait " crates/store/src/` returns nothing, so the crate has no trait convention to join, and a trait whose only second implementation is its own test fake does not clear the workshop-001 rule-3 bar that the frozen contract's own rustdoc cites to justify ITSELF. Build free async fns over &PgPool and put the dedupe/rotation DECISION in a pure core function, so the interesting tests need neither Postgres nor a fake. Named trigger, so this is a deferral and not a refusal: if the u4 orchestrator needs a PG-free seam, the trait is added then, on u4's evidence. This column is not part of the phase-1 freeze. (c) THE LEDGER STORES (harness, session_id, ordinal) -> turn_no, not a bare ordinal set: turn_no is the navigation axis (req-0026) and the idempotency key of the append, so a rescan that RECOVERS a record's existing number beats one that renumbers it, at identical row count. (d) parent_ordinal IS DROPPED and that is confirmed, not an oversight — fs3_core::conversation::Turn is {turn_no, role, source, head_sha, at, body, items} and holds no parent field. Say so in a comment where you drop it. (e) THE PAYLOAD POLICY IS WRITTEN ONCE, PUBLIC, IN CORE. shape(), WRITE_FAMILY, is_write_family(), first_line() and floor_char_boundary() are all PRIVATE to crates/daemon/src/conversations.rs, so implementing the policy again here would create the second copy that risk r3 names. Write it once in core; put the daemon delegation in your snap-in recipe as a line for the PM to paste; do not edit the daemon yourself.

PRIME RULING 2026-08-28, granting the daemon half of u8(e) — the payload policy MOVES once into fs3-core as public functions and the daemon's shape() delegates to it. Three conditions, all binding on this unit's work: (1) THE MOVE IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING and the EXISTING daemon intake tests prove it — they must stay green UNMODIFIED. If any of them needs an edit to pass, that is a behaviour change, not a move: STOP and tell the PM, who routes it to prime. (2) OUTPUT_HEAD_BYTES AND THE POLICY FUNCTIONS ARE SINGLE-SOURCED IN CORE; the daemon re-exports the constant if its public surface still needs it. No second definition of the constant anywhere. (3) THE COMPOSITION EDIT IS THE PM'S, NOT YOURS — you write the core policy and the snap-in recipe line; you never touch crates/daemon.
pij-traditional-piranha (the PM) is your ONLY upward interface: acks, questions, done reports. You never message prime (pij-instant-lynx) or Jordan directly unless my seat is dead.
DEFER to me: anything touching the frozen contract or its types, dependency additions, migration numbers, schema changes, another unit's paths, and anything in .harness/government/**.
YOURS to decide: your module's internal structure, your test names and helpers, the order you work the tasks, how you factor private helpers — as long as the contract and the fence hold.
Stop-and-ask with EVIDENCE beats guessing, and beats coding around a brief you believe is wrong. One question per message: one sentence of context, one sentence of ask.

value.fence: crates/store/src/ingest_cursors.rs (new) + its one module line in the store's lib.rs · crates/store/migrations/00NN_ingest_cursors.sql (NUMBER RE-VERIFIED, see u1) · crates/core/src/conversation_normalize.rs (new) + its one module line in core's lib.rs · docs/services/convo-cursors.md (new). NOTHING ELSE — in particular, no reader modules and no daemon/cli wiring. Your scratch database is fs3_convo_u2: export FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://flowspace3:flowspace3@127.0.0.1:5433/fs3_convo_u2 (already created for you).
value.forbidden_note: Never touch another unit's paths, the committed fixtures, .harness/government/**, the plan's flow state, or another seat's worktree. Never `docker compose up`. Never merge, never open a PR, never push to main — the PM composes.

value.text: THE LEDGER DEDUPES A RESCAN TO ZERO. A rescanned=true batch carrying the WHOLE conversation, after a first ingest already stored it, results in ZERO new turns. This is the case the unit exists for: silence here is indistinguishable from a burst of new turns and duplicates an entire conversation. (Ruled 2026-08-28 replacing a reader done-bar the PM copy-pasted into this packet; u2 implements no ConversationSource, owns no store and has no fixtures.)

THE CURSOR ROUND-TRIPS DURABLY for all three SourceCursor variants — ByteOffset, Seq and RowId — proven against the scratch database, not only in memory. A cursor that survives only inside one process makes the second ingest a full re-read.

THE NORMALIZER GOLDENS match the measured payload spec, with the truncation MUTATION-CHECKED: a golden that still passes when the 512-byte cut is removed is not a test. Includes an explicit multi-byte case proving the head lands on a CHARACTER boundary.
harness checks GREEN in your own worktree (fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --all), with FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL set to your scratch database.

THE SNAP-IN RECIPE is shipped with the unit (tenet 4): the exact wiring the PM will paste at the composition root — construction calls, the module lines, config shape — as a section in docs/services/convo-cursors.md. It also carries the line delegating the daemon's private shape() to the core payload policy, so the policy has ONE implementation rather than two. You write the recipe; you never wire it in yourself.

Done report to the PM: what shipped, the evidence (test names, counts), every deviation from this packet and why, and anything the composer must know. Include your observed rustc/cargo versions (tenet 10).
